summary: A 1971 note by Steve Crocker on distributing the notes through the Network Information Center. It was replaced by RFC 155.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 95 changes how Network Working Group notes are distributed. Each network site is to have a Technical Liaison Contact who receives the notes from the Network Information Center.

subtitle: A 1971 note routes network working group documents through designated site contacts.

tldr.problem: The Network Working Group mailing list duplicated parts of the Network Information Center's distribution system.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 95 presumes each site has a Technical Liaison Contact and directs that NWG notes be sent to those contacts and to mailing-list members not based at a site.
tldr.outcome: The note also allows authors to distribute directly if they inform the NIC and obtain mailing-list changes. It was replaced by RFC 155.

today: RFC 95 is historic and was obsoleted by RFC 155. It records early procedures for distributing Network Working Group notes through the NIC and site contacts.

sections.title: The NIC Distribution System
sections.content: RFC 95 describes the Network Information Center (NIC) at SRI as establishing communication lines with all network sites. Each site has a Station Agent to maintain a small library of NIC documents and a Technical Liaison Contact to connect network requests with people or services at that site.
sections.plainLanguage: The NIC sends documents to network sites. Each site has a person to receive and manage those documents.

sections.title: Who Receives NWG Notes
sections.content: RFC 95 presumes each site has a Technical Liaison Contact. If one has not been appointed, the current recipient of NWG notes for that site serves as the contact by default. NWG notes go to those contacts and to people on the mailing list who are not at a site.
sections.plainLanguage: Each site receives notes through its designated contact. If no one has been appointed, the current recipient becomes that contact by default.

sections.title: Numbering and Direct Distribution
sections.content: The RFC says Jeanne North at SRI will continue assigning RFC and NIC numbers. Authors may send notes to the NIC for distribution or distribute them directly, but an author distributing directly should notify Mrs. North and obtain any mailing-list changes. The note also lists telephone contacts for sites.
sections.plainLanguage: The NIC continues assigning numbers. An author may distribute a note directly but must coordinate the mailing-list details with the NIC.
